Fix \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(1\le\ell\le d_c\), and \(1\le f\le L\).  Write \(t=t_{c\ell}\), \(Q=Q_c\), \(G=G_c\), \(\overline Q=\widehat Q_{c,-f}\), and \(\overline G=\widehat G_{c,-f}\), and condition on the sigma-field \(\mathcal T_{cf}\) generated by the observations used to train the fold-specific learners.  By the cross-fitting construction, the validation observations are independent of \(\mathcal T_{cf}\).  The inverse-survival metric in Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-estimability} makes \(1/\overline G\) well defined on the required horizon with probability tending to one.  All survival quotients use the convention in Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score}.

For one validation observation, define
\[
 N(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\le u,\Delta=1\},
 \qquad
 Y(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\ge u\}.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring}, the event-wins-ties rule \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{T\le C\}\), and the left-continuous convention \(G(u\mid X)=P(C\ge u\mid X)\) give
\[
 E\{dN(u)\mid X\}=Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X)\Lambda(du\mid X),
 \qquad
 E\{Y(u)\mid X\}=Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} excludes an event atom at zero, matching the interval \((0,t]\) in Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score}.

We first record a quotient identity that also covers a survival curve reaching zero.  Set \(R=Q/\overline Q-1\), and let \(dR^{\circ}\) be the signed Stieltjes measure obtained from \(dR\) by deleting any jump at which \(\overline Q\) first reaches zero.  Away from such a jump, the product-integral equations imply
\[
 dR^{\circ}(u\mid X)
 =\frac{Q(u-\mid X)}{\overline Q(u\mid X)}
   (\overline\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X).
\]
Indeed, at a jump where both denominators are positive,
\[
 \Delta\!\left(\frac Q{\overline Q}\right)(u)
 =\frac{Q(u-)}{\overline Q(u)}
   \{\Delta\overline\Lambda(u)-\Delta\Lambda(u)\},
\]
and the continuous part is the ordinary quotient rule.  Assumption~\ref{ass:relative-survival-bv} makes \(R\) real-valued and of bounded variation.  Thus, if \(\overline Q\) reaches zero, \(Q\) is also zero there; at that point either both hazards jump to one, so their difference is zero, or \(Q(u-)=0\).  The deleted quotient-reset jump therefore contributes nothing to the hazard-difference measure.  Consequently
\[
 |dR^{\circ}|((0,t])\le |dR|((0,t])=V_{cf\ell}(X).
\]
Assumptions~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} and~\ref{ass:learner-origin-normalization} give \(R(0\mid X)=0\).  If \(\overline Q(t\mid X)>0\), integration of the quotient rule gives
\[
 Q(t\mid X)=\overline Q(t\mid X)
 \left\{1+\int_{(0,t]}dR^{\circ}(u\mid X)\right\}.
\]
If \(\overline Q(t\mid X)=0\), real-valuedness of \(R\) gives \(Q(t\mid X)=0\), so the same identity holds because both sides vanish.

Taking conditional expectations in Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score} and using the two compensator identities above gives
\[
 E\{\psi_t(O;\overline Q,\overline G)\mid X,\mathcal T_{cf}\}
 =\overline Q(t\mid X)
 \left[1+\int_{(0,t]}
 \frac{G(u\mid X)}{\overline G(u\mid X)}
 dR^{\circ}(u\mid X)\right].
\]
When \(\overline Q(t)>0\), this follows by factoring \(\overline Q(t)\) in the preceding quotient formula.  When \(\overline Q(t)=0\), terms before its first zero have multiplier \(\overline Q(t)/\overline Q(u)=0\), while the event-hazard difference at and after that zero vanishes by the preceding case analysis, so the displayed identity remains valid under the stated quotient convention.  Subtracting the product-integral identity yields the exact conditional bias
\[
 \mathfrak R_{cf\ell}(X)
 =\overline Q(t\mid X)
 \int_{(0,t]}
 \left\{\frac{G(u\mid X)}{\overline G(u\mid X)}-1\right\}
 dR^{\circ}(u\mid X).
\]
It is identically zero if either fitted nuisance equals its truth; hence neither nuisance has an uncancelled first-order contribution.

Define
\[
 A_{cf\ell}(X)=\sup_{0\le u\le t}
 \left|\frac1{\overline G(u\mid X)}-\frac1{G(u\mid X)}\right|.
\]
Since \(0\le\overline Q(t)\le1\), \(0\le G\le1\), and \(|dR^{\circ}|\le|dR|\),
\[
 |\mathfrak R_{cf\ell}(X)|
 \le A_{cf\ell}(X)V_{cf\ell}(X).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-estimability} gives \(\|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(b_K)\), and Assumption~\ref{ass:relative-survival-variation-rate} gives \(\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\), jointly over the fixed indices.  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and Assumption~\ref{ass:nuisance-product-rate} therefore give
\[
 \left|P_c\{\psi_t(\overline Q,\overline G)-\psi_t(Q,G)\}\right|
 \le \|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}\|V_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 =O_P(a_Kb_K)=o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]

It remains to control the fitted-score empirical term.  For \(0\le u\le t\), put
\[
 r_t(u\mid X)=\frac{Q(t\mid X)}{Q(u\mid X)},
 \qquad
 \overline r_t(u\mid X)=\frac{\overline Q(t\mid X)}{\overline Q(u\mid X)}.
\]
Under the \(0/0=1\) convention these paths are nondecreasing, lie in \([0,1]\), and satisfy \(d\overline r_t=\overline r_t\,d\overline\Lambda\), including a possible terminal jump to one.  With \(w=t\wedge U\), the score can therefore be written without an unpaired inverse event-survival factor as
\[
 \psi_t(O;\overline Q,\overline G)
 =\overline Q(t\mid X)
 -\mathbf 1\{U\le t,\Delta=1\}
  \frac{\overline r_t(U\mid X)}{\overline G(U\mid X)}
 +\int_{(0,w]}\frac1{\overline G(u\mid X)},d\overline r_t(u\mid X).
\]
Let
\[
 D_{Q,cf\ell}(X)=\sup_{0\le u\le t}
 |\overline r_t(u\mid X)-r_t(u\mid X)|.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:event-estimability} gives \(\|D_{Q,cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-positivity} gives \(1/G\le g^{-1}\); moreover \(1/G\) is nondecreasing and has total variation at most \(g^{-1}-1\).  Split the difference of the two integral terms as
\[
 \int\left(\frac1{\overline G}-\frac1G\right)d\overline r_t
 +\int\frac1G,d(\overline r_t-r_t).
\]
The first term is bounded by \(A_{cf\ell}(X)\), since \(\operatorname{TV}(\overline r_t)\le1\).  Stieltjes integration by parts bounds the second by its two endpoint terms plus
\(D_{Q,cf\ell}(X)\operatorname{TV}(1/G)\), hence by \(C_gD_{Q,cf\ell}(X)\) for a finite constant depending only on \(g\).  The baseline difference is bounded by \(D_{Q,cf\ell}(X)\), because both true and fitted survival equal one at the origin, and the event term obeys the same \(C_gD_{Q,cf\ell}+A_{cf\ell}\) bound.  Therefore
\[
 \|\psi_t(\overline Q,\overline G)-\psi_t(Q,G)\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le C_g\{\|D_{Q,cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
             +\|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}\}
 =O_P(a_K+b_K)=o_P(1),
\]
where the last equality uses Assumptions~\ref{ass:event-rate-vanishes} and~\ref{ass:censor-rate-vanishes}.

Let \(n_{cf}=|\mathcal V_{cf}|\), let \(\mathbb P_{cf}\) be the validation empirical measure, and abbreviate \(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}=\psi_t(\mathord\cdot;\overline Q,\overline G)\) and \(\psi_{c\ell}=\psi_t(\mathord\cdot;Q,G)\).  Empty folds contribute zero.  Since the folds partition \(\{1,\ldots,K\}\), Definition~\ref{def:cell-estimator} and the identity \(P_c\psi_{c\ell}=S_c(t)\), obtained above by setting both nuisances to their truths, give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_{c\ell}(O_{ci})\\
 &\quad+\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{n_{cf}}K
 (\mathbb P_{cf}-P_c)(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell})\\
 &\quad+\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{n_{cf}}K
 P_c(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}).
\end{aligned}
\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid}, conditionally on \(\mathcal T_{cf}\), the validation observations are independent with law \(P_c\).  The conditional standard deviation of the \(f\)-th weighted empirical term is at most
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{n_{cf}}}{K}
 \|\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le K^{-1/2}o_P(1).
\]
Conditional Chebyshev and fixed \(L\) make the empirical sum \(o_P(K^{-1/2})\).  The bias sum is \(O_P(a_Kb_K)=o_P(K^{-1/2})\).  Consequently
\[
 \sqrt K\{\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)\}
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_{c\ell}(O_{ci})+o_P(1).
\]

Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} makes the numbers of cells, folds, and coordinates fixed, so a finite union bound makes all preceding rates joint.  Assumption~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} permits pairing the common within-cell index and stacking the cell influences as \(\Phi_i\).  Extracting the four blocks gives the asserted expansion for \((\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\).

For an observation in fold \(f\), define
\[
 \widehat\phi_{c\ell,i}
 =\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}(O_{ci})-\widehat s_{c\ell}.
\]
The expansion gives \(|\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)|=o_P(1)\), while the fitted-score bound gives \(\|\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=o_P(1)\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment} supplies the finite second moment of the true centered score.  The triangle inequality therefore yields
\[
 \|\widehat\phi_{c\ell}-\phi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le \|\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
     +|\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)|=o_P(1).
\]
A final finite union bound proves joint foldwise \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistency.  This proves the lemma.  No step above claims that generic nuisance consistency implies the separately imposed path-variation restrictions.

Let \(M=U\Sigma V^\top\) be a compact singular-value decomposition, with orthonormal-column matrices \(U\in\mathbb R^{N_0\times r}\), \(V\in\mathbb R^{T_0\times r}\), and \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)\).  Assumptions~\ref{ass:exact-rank} and~\ref{ass:singular-gap} give \(\sigma_r\ge\kappa>0\) and \(\sigma_{r+1}=0\).  The variational characterization of singular values gives
\[
 |\sigma_k(M+H)-\sigma_k(M)|\le\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Thus, when \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\kappa/3\), the leading \(r\)-dimensional singular subspaces remain separated from their complements.

Choose orthogonal complements \(U_\perp,V_\perp\) and write
\[
 U^\top HV=H_{11},\quad U^\top HV_\perp=H_{12},\quad
 U_\perp^\top HV=H_{21},\quad U_\perp^\top HV_\perp=H_{22}.
\]
Differentiating the equations defining the two separated singular subspaces, or equivalently multiplying the first-order perturbation by the four pairs of orthogonal projectors, gives
\[
 D(M\mapsto M_r)_M[H]
 =UH_{11}V^\top+UH_{12}V_\perp^\top+U_\perp H_{21}V^\top.
\]
The normal block \(H_{22}\) is absent to first order.  Since \(P=M^+=V\Sigma^{-1}U^\top\), differentiating the inverse nonzero singular block and both singular subspaces gives
\[
 D(M_r^+)_M[H]
 =-V\Sigma^{-1}H_{11}\Sigma^{-1}U^\top
 +V\Sigma^{-2}H_{21}^\top U_\perp^\top
 +V_\perp H_{12}^\top\Sigma^{-2}U^\top.
\]
Every displayed term is linear in \(H\).  The identities
\[
 MP=UU^\top,\qquad PM=VV^\top,\qquad
 PP^\top=V\Sigma^{-2}V^\top,
 \qquad P^\top P=U\Sigma^{-2}U^\top
\]
turn the last display into
\[
 D(M_r^+)_M[H]
 =-PHP+PP^\top H^\top(I-MP)+(I-PM)H^\top P^\top P
 =\mathcal L_M(H).
\]
This holds for every ambient perturbation \(H\), because its omitted normal block has zero derivative.  Finally, finite-dimensional matrix multiplication is bilinear, so the product rule applied to \(\mathcal F(y,M,B)=yM_r^+B\) yields
\[
 D\mathcal F_{(y,M,B)}[h_y,H,h_B]
 =h_yPB+y\mathcal L_M(H)B+yPh_B.
\]
The separated spectral projectors, inversion of the nonzero \(r\times r\) block, and matrix multiplication have uniformly quadratic remainders on a smaller gap neighborhood.  The derivative is therefore Fr\'echet, and it contains all three learned-block perturbations and both projector corrections.

Let \(Z=(y,M,B,s_1)\), with matrix blocks vectorized in a fixed order, and let \(\widehat Z=(\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} makes this dimension fixed.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} gives
\[
 \widehat Z-Z=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_i+r_K,
 \qquad \sqrt K\|r_K\|_2\to_P0.
\]
Every component of \(\Phi_i\) is centered.  Assumptions~\ref{ass:cell-iid} and~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} make \(\Phi_1,\ldots,\Phi_K\) independent and identically distributed, with common law equal to the product of the fixed cell laws.  Assumptions~\ref{ass:influence-moment} and~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} imply
\[
 E\Phi_i=0,
 \qquad E\|\Phi_i\|_2^{2+\nu}<\infty.
\]
Thus \(E\|K^{-1/2}\sum_i\Phi_i\|_2^2=E\|\Phi_i\|_2^2<\infty\), and Markov's inequality gives
\[
 \|\widehat Z-Z\|_2=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad \|\widehat M-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]

Assumption~\ref{ass:exact-rank} gives \(M_r=M\), while Assumption~\ref{ass:singular-gap} gives \(\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sigma_r(M)^{-1}\le\kappa^{-1}\).  Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential} supplies a neighborhood of \((y,M,B)\) on which \(\mathcal F\) is Fr\'echet differentiable.  Since \(\widehat Z\to_PZ\), the estimated blocks lie in that neighborhood with probability tending to one.  Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map}, the derivative, and the root-\(K\) rate yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\theta-\theta
 &=(\widehat y-y)PB+y\mathcal L_M(\widehat M-M)B+yP(\widehat B-B)+o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \{\Phi_{y,i}PB+y\mathcal L_M(\Phi_{M,i})B+yP\Phi_{B,i}\}
 +o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\theta,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The factual-post block of Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} is
\[
 \widehat s_1-s_1=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{1,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Stacking and applying Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} proves the asserted asymptotic linear representation.

Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} expresses \(\Phi_{\eta,i}\) as a fixed linear transformation of \(\Phi_i\).  Its coefficients are finite because the dimensions are fixed, \(\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa^{-1}\), and Definition~\ref{def:full-differential} makes \(\mathcal L_M\) bounded.  Hence
\[
 E\Phi_{\eta,i}=0,
 \qquad E\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^{2+\nu}<\infty,
 \qquad E(\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top)=\Omega_\eta.
\]
For any \(a\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), let \(W_i=a^\top\Phi_{\eta,i}\), \(\omega_a^2=a^\top\Omega_\eta a\), and \(\delta=\min(\nu,1)>0\).  The elementary Taylor bound
\[
 \left|e^{\mathrm ix}-1-\mathrm ix+\frac{x^2}{2}\right|
 \le C_\delta|x|^{2+\delta}
\]
and the preceding moment condition imply
\[
 \left|Ee^{\mathrm iW_i/\sqrt K}-1+\frac{\omega_a^2}{2K}\right|
 \le C_\delta K^{-1-\delta/2}E|W_i|^{2+\delta}=o(K^{-1}).
\]
Independence therefore gives
\[
 E\exp\!\left\{\mathrm ia^\top K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\right\}
 \longrightarrow \exp(-\omega_a^2/2).
\]
This is the characteristic function of \(\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta)\), including when \(\Omega_\eta\) is singular.  The continuity theorem for characteristic functions and the asymptotic linear representation prove the joint limit.  No covariance lower bound is used.

For the plug-in conclusions, let \(\Pi_R(A)\) be the projector onto the leading \(r\) right singular vectors of a matrix \(A\) near \(M\).  The singular-value bound
\[
 |\sigma_j(A)-\sigma_j(M)|\le\|A-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
and the fixed gap make that subspace unique locally.  The set of rank-\(r\) projectors is compact, and \(\Pi_R(A)\) uniquely maximizes \(Q\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(QA^\top A)\) locally.  Thus every subsequential limit as \(A\to M\) equals \(\Pi_R(M)\), proving \(\Pi_R(A)\to\Pi_R(M)\) and \(A_r=A\Pi_R(A)\to M\).  Moreover,
\[
 A_r^+=\{A_r^\top A_r+I-\Pi_R(A)\}^{-1}A_r^\top.
\]
The matrix in braces has eigenvalues \(\sigma_1(A)^2,\ldots,\sigma_r(A)^2,1,\ldots,1\), uniformly bounded away from zero near \(M\).  Continuity of multiplication and inversion, followed by substitution into Definition~\ref{def:full-differential}, yields
\[
 (\widehat M)_r^+\to_PP,
 \qquad \widehat{\mathcal L}_{\widehat M}\to_P\mathcal L_M
\]
in the relevant operator norms.

Let \(\widehat\Phi_i\) stack the fold-specific fitted cell influences.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} gives foldwise \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistency.  For each fold, conditional Markov's inequality applied to its validation observations, followed by a finite union bound, gives
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\|_2^2=o_P(1).
\]
Let \(\mathsf A\) be the fixed linear operator in Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence}, including the unchanged factual-post block, and let \(\widehat{\mathsf A}\) be its plug-in version.  Consistency of the four blocks and the preceding spectral convergences imply
\[
 \|\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),
 \qquad \|\widehat{\mathsf A}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(1).
\]
Also \(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_i\|_2^2=O_P(1)\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2
 &\le2\|\widehat{\mathsf A}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 K^{-1}\sum_i\|\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\|_2^2\\
 &\quad+2\|\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_i\|_2^2=o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]

Put \(D_i=\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\).  Expanding outer products and applying Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left\|\widehat\Omega_\eta-K^{-1}\sum_i
 \Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le\left(K^{-1}\sum_i\|D_i\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}\\
 &\quad\times\left[
 \left(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
 +\left(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
 \right]=o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Each coordinate product of \(\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\) is integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz.  The scalar weak law applied entrywise, with fixed \(2J\), gives
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_i\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\to_P\Omega_\eta.
\]
The last two displays prove \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\to_P\Omega_\eta\), without requiring invertibility.

Finally, Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion}, under conditional independent censoring and censor positivity, centers each cell estimator at the covariate-standardized event survival \(S_c(t)=E\{Q_c(t\mid X_{ci})\}\).  Hence \(y,M,B,s_1\) are observed-law identified survival blocks, rather than marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-targets.  Assumption~\ref{ass:post-transport}, by itself, states that the target unit's untreated post-treatment survival row equals the observed-law functional \(yM_r^+B\).  This assumption, not the definition of \(\theta\), supplies the causal equality.  The target-pre row-space assumption is not used.  The factual row \(s_1\) remains the treated post-period survival curve.  This proves the theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose that, for every \(c\in\mathcal C\), the support \(\mathcal X_c\) of \(X_{ci}\) and the set \(\mathcal T_c\) of event times not exceeding the largest required horizon are fixed and finite.  Suppose there are fixed constants \(\pi_0,\varepsilon_0,\rho>0\) such that
\[
 P_c(X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge s)\ge\pi_0,
 \qquad
 h_c(s\mid x):=P_c(T_{ci}=s\mid T_{ci}\ge s,X_{ci}=x)\le1-\varepsilon_0
\]
for all \(c\), \(x\in\mathcal X_c\), and \(s\in\mathcal T_c\) on the required horizon, and such that every training complement \(\mathcal I_{cf}^-:=\{1,\ldots,K\}\setminus\mathcal V_{cf}\) has size at least \(\rho K\).  Define
\[
 \widetilde h_{cf}(s\mid x)=
 \frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{cf}^-}
       \mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}=s,\Delta_{ci}=1\}}
      {\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{cf}^-}
       \mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge s\}},
\]
with value zero when its denominator is zero, let
\[
 \widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)
 =\min\{1-\varepsilon_0/2,\max(0,\widetilde h_{cf}(s\mid x))\},
 \qquad
 \widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid x)
 =\prod_{s\in\mathcal T_c:s\le u}\{1-\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)\},
\]
and set \(\widehat Q_{c,-f}(0\mid x)=1\).  Then, uniformly over the fixed cells, folds, strata, event times, and required grid coordinates,
\[
 \left|\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)-h_c(s\mid x)\right|=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{TV}_{[0,t_{c\ell}]}
 \log\!\left\{\frac{Q_c(\mathord\cdot\mid x)}
                       {\widehat Q_{c,-f}(\mathord\cdot\mid x)}\right\}
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Consequently \(R_{cf}(\mathord\cdot\mid x)\) is of bounded variation,
\[
 \max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X_{ci})\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
and
\[
 \max_{c,f,\ell}
 \left\|
  \sup_{0\le u\le t_{c\ell}}
  \left|
   \frac{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(t_{c\ell}\mid X_{ci})}
        {\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid X_{ci})}
   -\frac{Q_c(t_{c\ell}\mid X_{ci})}{Q_c(u\mid X_{ci})}
  \right|
 \right\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Thus this finite-stratum learner satisfies the event-side restrictions with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\), and every censor learner with \(b_K=o(1)\) satisfies \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\).  This is an attainability certificate for the stated finite-stratum submodel only, not for generic learners or for the TCL application without verification of these conditions.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(c\), \(f\), \(x\in\mathcal X_c\), and \(s\in\mathcal T_c\), and write \(n=|\mathcal I_{cf}^-|\).  The training indices are fixed independently of the observations by the cross-fitting construction, so Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid} makes the \(n\) training observations independent with law \(P_c\).  Put
\[
 A_i=\mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}=s,\Delta_{ci}=1\},
 \qquad
 D_i=\mathbf 1\{X_{ci}=x,U_{ci}\ge s\}.
\]
The event-wins-ties definition of \(\Delta_{ci}\) gives
\[
 \{U_{ci}=s,\Delta_{ci}=1\}=\{T_{ci}=s,C_{ci}\ge s\},
 \qquad
 \{U_{ci}\ge s\}=\{T_{ci}\ge s,C_{ci}\ge s\}.
\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring}, conditional on \(X_{ci}=x\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 p_1&:=E_{P_c}A_i
 =P_c(X_{ci}=x)P_c(T_{ci}=s\mid X_{ci}=x)G_c(s\mid x),\\
 p_0&:=E_{P_c}D_i
 =P_c(X_{ci}=x)P_c(T_{ci}\ge s\mid X_{ci}=x)G_c(s\mid x).
\end{aligned}
\]
The assumed at-risk bound gives \(p_0\ge\pi_0\), and division is therefore valid.  Cancelling the common censor-survival factor yields
\[
 \frac{p_1}{p_0}=P_c(T_{ci}=s\mid T_{ci}\ge s,X_{ci}=x)=h_c(s\mid x).
\]

Let \(\overline A=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{cf}^-}A_i\) and \(\overline D=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{cf}^-}D_i\).  Since both summands lie in \([0,1]\), Chebyshev's inequality gives
\[
 \overline A-p_1=O_P(n^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \overline D-p_0=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
There are only finitely many cells, folds, strata, and event times by Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} and the finite-support premise, so a union bound makes both rates uniform.  Because \(n\ge\rho K\), they are \(O_P(K^{-1/2})\).  On the event \(|\overline D-p_0|\le\pi_0/2\), whose probability tends to one uniformly, \(\overline D\ge\pi_0/2\) and
\[
 \left|\frac{\overline A}{\overline D}-\frac{p_1}{p_0}\right|
 \le \frac{2}{\pi_0}|\overline A-p_1|
     +\frac{2p_1}{\pi_0^2}|\overline D-p_0|
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Thus the zero-denominator convention is used only on an event with probability tending to zero.  Projection onto \([0,1-\varepsilon_0/2]\) is nonexpansive and the true hazard belongs to \([0,1-\varepsilon_0]\), so
\[
 \max_{c,f,x,s}|\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)-h_c(s\mid x)|=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]

Assumption~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} and the finite event-time support imply the conditional product representation
\[
 Q_c(u\mid x)=\prod_{s\in\mathcal T_c:s\le u}\{1-h_c(s\mid x)\}.
\]
The constructed learner has the analogous finite product and equals one at the origin.  Define
\[
 A_{cf}(u\mid x)
 =\log\!\left\{\frac{Q_c(u\mid x)}{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid x)}\right\}
 =\sum_{s\in\mathcal T_c:s\le u}
  [\log\{1-h_c(s\mid x)\}-\log\{1-\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)\}].
\]
The true factors are at least \(\varepsilon_0\), and clipping makes the estimated factors at least \(\varepsilon_0/2\).  The mean-value theorem therefore bounds every summand in absolute value by
\[
 \frac{2}{\varepsilon_0}
 |\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)-h_c(s\mid x)|.
\]
The path \(A_{cf}\) has only the fixed finite set of possible jumps \(\mathcal T_c\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{TV}_{[0,t_{c\ell}]}(A_{cf})
 \le\frac{2}{\varepsilon_0}
 \sum_{s\in\mathcal T_c:s\le t_{c\ell}}
 |\widehat h_{cf}(s\mid x)-h_c(s\mid x)|
 =O_P(K^{-1/2})
\]
uniformly over all displayed indices.  This proves the log-total-variation assertion and also \(\sup_u|A_{cf}(u\mid x)|=O_P(K^{-1/2})\).

Because \(R_{cf}=\exp(A_{cf})-1\), composition of a bounded-variation path with the exponential map gives
\[
 V_{cf\ell}(x)
 \le \exp\{\sup_{0\le u\le t_{c\ell}}|A_{cf}(u\mid x)|\}
      \operatorname{TV}_{[0,t_{c\ell}]}(A_{cf})
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
The paths have finitely many jumps and strictly positive product factors, so bounded variation holds for every training sample, not merely asymptotically.  Since every \(\mathcal X_c\) is fixed and finite,
\[
 \|V_{cf\ell}(X_{ci})\|_{L_2(P_c)}
 \le\max_{x\in\mathcal X_c}V_{cf\ell}(x)
 =O_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
uniformly over the fixed indices.

Finally, for \(0\le u\le t=t_{c\ell}\),
\[
 \log\!\left[
  \frac{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(t\mid x)/\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid x)}
       {Q_c(t\mid x)/Q_c(u\mid x)}
 \right]
 =-\{A_{cf}(t\mid x)-A_{cf}(u\mid x)\}.
\]
The absolute value of the right-hand side is bounded by \(\operatorname{TV}_{[0,t]}(A_{cf})\).  All four survival ratios lie in \([0,1]\), and the elementary bound \(|e^z-1|\le e^{|z|}|z|\) consequently yields the stated uniform \(O_P(K^{-1/2})\) ratio error.  Passing to \(L_2(P_c)\) again uses only the fixed finite covariate supports.  Taking \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\) proves both event-side rates, and if \(b_K=o(1)\), then
\[
 a_Kb_K=K^{-1/2}b_K=o(K^{-1/2}).
\]
This completes the finite-stratum certificate.

open_obligations.partial_result:
In a fixed-dimensional orthogonal cell-score experiment, let \(\rho_K\) be a consistently estimable operator-norm noise scale with \(\|\widehat M-M_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(\rho_K)\).  If the cell expansion and influence estimation are uniform over a declared triangular collection, the larger singular values remain uniformly separated, and standardized moments and relevant variances are uniformly controlled, then ordinary selected-rank spectral inference is uniformly regular on the unrestricted active-loading region
\[
 \Delta_K/\rho_K\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
For any \(h_K\to\infty\) satisfying \(h_K\rho_K/\Delta_K\to0\), thresholding at \(h_K\widehat\rho_K\) selects rank \(r\) uniformly with probability tending to one; the differentiated plug-in and Gaussian-multiplier band are then uniformly valid for \(y(M_K)_r^+B\).  For the Tikhonov inverse
\[
 P_{\lambda,K}=(M_K^\top M_K+\lambda_K^2I)^{-1}M_K^\top,
\]
the exact bias relative to the unregularized target is
\[
 yP_{\lambda,K}B-y(M_K)_r^+B
 =-\sum_{k=1}^r
 \frac{\lambda_K^2}{\sigma_{k,K}^2+\lambda_K^2}
 \frac{yv_{k,K}}{\sigma_{k,K}}u_{k,K}^\top B.
\]
Thus regularization does not enlarge the unrestricted frontier unless this bias is included or is negligible relative to the standard error.  The frontier cannot be a function of \(\Delta_K\) alone on restricted loading classes: if the weak component \((yv_{r,K}/\sigma_{r,K})u_{r,K}^\top B\) vanishes identically, rank-\((r-1)\) inference targets the same curve and remains regular.  Conversely, on an unrestricted class allowing an active weak component, mutually contiguous two-path alternatives with \(\Delta_K\asymp\rho_K\) and fixed target separation rule out uniformly consistent estimation and any uniformly honest band whose diameter vanishes.  The finite-stratum certificate in Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-stratum-hazard-certificate} supplies a pointwise fixed-cell learner example, but it does not supply the uniform triangular experiment, observable operator-noise calibration, loading class, or uniform moment and variance conditions needed to turn this conditional frontier into a resolution of the open-ended question.

prose_updates.tldr: For fixed donor count, pre grid, post grid, rank, and a separated nonzero singular spectrum, covariate-adjusted cross-fitted AIPCW cell estimates have a joint root-\(K\) expansion conditional on explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation-rate restrictions on fitted event-survival paths. A clipped empirical discrete-hazard learner verifies those restrictions at rate \(K^{-1/2}\) on a finite-stratum submodel with positive at-risk probabilities and hazards bounded away from one; this certificate does not validate generic learners or the TCL application. Differentiating the target-pre, donor-pre, and donor-post blocks yields a joint Gaussian law that may be singular. Nonzero counterfactual marginal variances suffice for the simultaneous band, and a separate nonzero grid-RMST variance suffices for scalar studentization. Post-transport alone supplies the causal equality for the joint theorem; target-pre span remains relevant only to the Han--Shah embedding and the converse subclass. Weak-gap and selected-rank inference remains open.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The joint cell and spectral results cover a fixed-panel, fixed-grid, exact-rank, fixed-singular-gap, exact-post-transport class. They additionally require within-cell i.i.d. sampling, cross-cell independence, conditional independent censoring, censor positivity, fixed-fold nuisance consistency and product rate, event-origin normalization, and the primitive bounded-variation and relative-variation-rate restrictions on the event learner. Full positive definiteness of \(\Omega_\eta\) is not required: the joint theorem allows a singular Gaussian law, while the band needs only positive counterfactual coordinate variances and the grid-RMST interval needs only its scalar influence variance. The finite-stratum certificate verifies the event-side learner restrictions only when covariates and event times have fixed finite support, observed at-risk masses are uniformly positive, event hazards are bounded away from one, and every training complement has size at least a fixed fraction of \(K\). proofs.proof_tex:
We first establish the probability limit and the continuity assertion. For a cell \(c\) and a time \(u\) in a fixed finite support, define the empirical event submass and empirical risk probability by
\[
 \widehat d_{cK}(u)=\frac1K\sum_{i=1}^K
       \mathbf 1\{U_{ci}=u,\Delta_{ci}=1\},\qquad
 \widehat R_{cK}(u)=\frac1K\sum_{i=1}^K
       \mathbf 1\{U_{ci}\ge u\},
\]
and let \(d_c(u)\) and \(R_c(u)\) denote their expectations under \(P_c\). By the within-cell i.i.d. sampling assumption, each summand is Bernoulli and hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\{\widehat d_{cK}(u)\}\le \frac{1}{4K},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}\{\widehat R_{cK}(u)\}\le \frac{1}{4K}.
\]
Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), Chebyshev's inequality, obtained by applying Markov's inequality to the squared centered mean, gives
\[
 P_c\!\left(\left|\widehat d_{cK}(u)-d_c(u)\right|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{1}{4K\varepsilon^2},\qquad
 P_c\!\left(\left|\widehat R_{cK}(u)-R_c(u)\right|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{1}{4K\varepsilon^2}.
\]
The fixed-panel assumption makes the total number of cells and retained coordinates finite. A finite union bound therefore yields joint convergence of all these empirical submasses and risk probabilities. Wherever \(R_c(u)>0\), division is continuous, and thus the empirical Kaplan--Meier product satisfies
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{cK}(t_{c\ell})
 =\prod_{u\le t_{c\ell}}
   \left\{1-\frac{\widehat d_{cK}(u)}{\widehat R_{cK}(u)}\right\}
 \ \xrightarrow{p}\ 
 \prod_{u\le t_{c\ell}}
   \left\{1-\frac{d_c(u)}{R_c(u)}\right\}
 =\widetilde S_c(t_{c\ell}).
\]
This directly verifies, rather than assumes, the cellwise probability-limit assertion on the finite discrete submodel. In the general product-integral version of the definition, \(\widetilde S_c\) is precisely the corresponding cellwise marginal Kaplan--Meier probability limit; the remainder of this argument only uses convergence at the fixed retained coordinates. Extracting blocks is linear, so the fixed number of coordinatewise limits gives
\[
 (\widehat y^{\mathrm{KM}},\widehat M^{\mathrm{KM}},
   \widehat B^{\mathrm{KM}})
 \xrightarrow{p}(\widetilde y,\widetilde M,\widetilde B).
\]

For completeness, we verify the needed spectral continuity. Let \(A_n\to A\) in operator norm and suppose
\[
 \sigma_r(A)>\sigma_{r+1}(A),
\]
where a missing singular value is interpreted as zero. The variational characterization of singular values and the triangle inequality give, directly,
\[
 |\sigma_k(A_n)-\sigma_k(A)|\le \|A_n-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
for every \(k\). Let \(\Pi_n\) be the orthogonal projector onto the leading \(r\) right singular subspace of \(A_n\). The set of rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors is compact. Every convergent subsequence of \((\Pi_n)\) has a limit maximizing
\[
 Q\longmapsto \operatorname{tr}(Q A^\top A)
\]
over rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors, because \(\Pi_n\) maximizes the analogous criterion with \(A_n^\top A_n\). The displayed strict singular gap makes this maximizer unique: it is the projector \(\Pi\) onto the leading \(r\) right singular subspace of \(A\). Thus every convergent subsequence has limit \(\Pi\), and compactness implies \(\Pi_n\to\Pi\). It follows that
\[
 (A_n)_r=A_n\Pi_n\longrightarrow A\Pi=A_r.
\]
Moreover, \(\sigma_r(A)>0\), so for all sufficiently large \(n\) the matrix
\[
 (A_n)_r^\top(A_n)_r+I-\Pi_n
\]
is invertible. A singular-value decomposition verifies the identity
\[
 (A_n)_r^+
 =\left\{(A_n)_r^\top(A_n)_r+I-\Pi_n\right\}^{-1}(A_n)_r^\top.
\]
Matrix inversion is continuous at an invertible matrix, and hence
\[
 (A_n)_r^+\longrightarrow A_r^+.
\]
Applying this fact at \(A=\widetilde M\), whose separated rank means the displayed strict gap, and then applying continuity of matrix multiplication proves
\[
 \widehat y^{\mathrm{KM}}
       (\widehat M^{\mathrm{KM}})_r^+
       \widehat B^{\mathrm{KM}}
 \xrightarrow{p}
 \widetilde y(\widetilde M)_r^+\widetilde B.
\]

Now parameterize the finite discrete submodel by its finitely many cell-atom probabilities. Each true survival coordinate is a finite sum of event atom probabilities. Each marginal Kaplan--Meier coordinate is a finite product of ratios of affine functions of the atom probabilities. It is therefore continuous wherever every risk denominator is positive. The preceding spectral argument shows that the two maps \(M\mapsto M_r^+\) and \(\widetilde M\mapsto(\widetilde M)_r^+\) are continuous wherever their rank-\(r\) singular gaps are positive. Hence the discrepancy map
\[
 p\longmapsto
 \beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(p)
 =\widetilde y(p)(\widetilde M(p))_r^+\widetilde B(p)
  -y(p)(M(p))_r^+B(p)
\]
is continuous on that domain. If \(\mathcal S\) denotes the finite-support conditional-censoring, positivity, exact-rank, and exact-transport submodel, then
\[
 \mathcal U=
 \left\{p\in\mathcal S:
   \begin{array}{l}
   \text{all required risks are positive, the true and naive rank-\(r\)}\\
   \text{singular gaps are positive, and }\|\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(p)\|_2>0
   \end{array}
 \right\}
\]
is the intersection of \(\mathcal S\) with an open set in the ambient finite-dimensional probability simplex. Thus \(\mathcal U\) is relatively open in \(\mathcal S\). This is the asserted open subclass on which the well-defined unadjusted PCR probability limit differs from the transported causal curve \(\theta=yM_r^+B\); the equality with that causal curve uses the exact post-transport assumption and is not part of the definition of the naive functional.

It remains to verify that the stated witness belongs to \(\mathcal U\). Its six displayed true survival pairs, with the repeated factual-post pair retained, are
\[
 (a,b)\in
 \left\{(7/10,9/20),(4/5,3/5),(3/5,3/10),
 (7/10,2/5),(1/2,1/5),(7/10,2/5)\right\}.
\]
For \(\epsilon_x=2x-1\), the three conditional event atom masses in the definition of \(P^\star\) obey, uniformly over this list and \(x\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 1-a-\frac{\epsilon_x}{20}\ge\frac3{20},\qquad
 a-b+\frac{\epsilon_x}{40}\ge\frac7{40},\qquad
 b+\frac{\epsilon_x}{40}\ge\frac7{40}.
\]
They sum to one. The three censor atom masses are, for \(x=0\),
\[
 (1-\gamma_{10},\gamma_{10}-\gamma_{20},\gamma_{20})
 =(1/5,3/10,1/2),
\]
and, for \(x=1\),
\[
 (1-\gamma_{11},\gamma_{11}-\gamma_{21},\gamma_{21})
 =(2/5,1/5,2/5).
\]
Thus every displayed atom mass is strictly positive. Conditional independent censoring holds because the construction draws \(T_{ci}\) and \(C_{ci}\) independently conditional on \(X_{ci}\). Also
\[
 P_c(T_{ci}>t_{c1}\mid X_{ci}=x)=a+\frac{\epsilon_x}{20},
 \qquad
 P_c(T_{ci}>t_{c2}\mid X_{ci}=x)=b+\frac{\epsilon_x}{40}.
\]
Since \(P_c(X_{ci}=0)=P_c(X_{ci}=1)=1/2\), averaging over \(X_{ci}\) gives the advertised marginal event-survival pair \((a,b)\). Finally, for every \(0\le t\le t_{c2}\),
\[
 G_c(t\mid x)=P_c(C_{ci}\ge t\mid X_{ci}=x)
 \ge P_c(C_{ci}=\infty\mid X_{ci}=x)
 =\gamma_{2x}\ge\frac25,
\]
which proves censoring positivity on the required horizon.

We next calculate the marginal Kaplan--Meier functional under the event-wins-ties convention \(\Delta_{ci}=\mathbf 1\{T_{ci}\le C_{ci}\}\). At the first time,
\[
 R_c(t_{c1})=P_c(U_{ci}\ge t_{c1})=1,
 \qquad
 d_c(t_{c1})=P_c(U_{ci}=t_{c1},\Delta_{ci}=1)=1-a.
\]
At the second time, conditional independence and the two covariate strata give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_c(t_{c2})
 &=\frac12\left\{(a-1/20)\frac45+(a+1/20)\frac35\right\}\\
 &=\frac{140a-1}{200},
 \end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_c(t_{c2})
 &=\frac12\left\{(a-b-1/40)\frac45
                   +(a-b+1/40)\frac35\right\}\\
 &=\frac{280(a-b)-1}{400}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The smallest displayed value of \(a\) is \(1/2\), so
\[
 R_c(t_{c2})\ge\frac{140(1/2)-1}{200}=\frac{69}{200}>0.
\]
The first Kaplan--Meier factor is \(1-(1-a)=a\), and the second gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widetilde S_c(t_{c2})
 &=a\left\{1-
   \frac{[280(a-b)-1]/400}{(140a-1)/200}\right\}\\
 &=a\left\{1-\frac{280(a-b)-1}{280a-2}\right\}
 =\frac{a(280b-1)}{280a-2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the marginal Kaplan--Meier pair is exactly
\[
 \left(a,\frac{a(280b-1)}{280a-2}\right).
\]
Substitution of the six pairs gives
\[
 \widetilde y=(7/10,175/388),\qquad
 \widetilde M=
 \begin{pmatrix}4/5&334/555\\3/5&3/10\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \widetilde B=
 \begin{pmatrix}7/10&777/1940\\1/2&55/276\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The factual-post pair is the repeated pair \((7/10,2/5)\), so its naive limit is \((7/10,777/1940)\), and it is not an argument of the counterfactual map in the definition of \(\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}\).

For the true donor-pre matrix,
\[
 \det(M)=\frac45\frac3{10}-\frac35\frac35=-\frac3{25}\ne0.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r=2\), its rank gap is positive, and its row space is all of \(\mathbb R^2\), so the target-pre-span condition holds. Direct inversion gives
\[
 yM^{-1}=(1/2,1/2),\qquad
 yM^{-1}B=(1/2,1/2)
 \begin{pmatrix}7/10&2/5\\1/2&1/5\end{pmatrix}
 =(3/5,3/10).
\]
The witness assigns its latent untreated target-post row to this last vector, so the exact post-transport condition holds and \(\theta=(3/5,3/10)\). For the naive donor-pre matrix,
\[
 \det(\widetilde M)
 =\frac45\frac3{10}-\frac35\frac{334}{555}
 =-\frac{112}{925}\ne0.
\]
Hence the naive rank-two gap is also positive and \((\widetilde M)_2^+=\widetilde M^{-1}\). Exact elimination yields
\[
 \widetilde y\widetilde M^{-1}
 =\left(\frac{777}{1552},\frac{581}{1164}\right).
\]
Multiplying by \(\widetilde B\) coordinate by coordinate gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widetilde y\widetilde M^{-1}\widetilde B
 &=\left(
 \frac{777}{1552}\frac7{10}+\frac{581}{1164}\frac12,
 \frac{777}{1552}\frac{777}{1940}
       +\frac{581}{1164}\frac{55}{276}
 \right)\\
 &=\left(\frac{27937}{46560},
          \frac{186964603}{623252160}\right)\\
 &=\left(\frac35+\frac1{46560},
          \frac3{10}-\frac{2209}{124650432}\right).
 \end{aligned}
\]
By the definition of \(\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}\),
\[
 \beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(P^\star)
 =\left(\frac1{46560},-\frac{2209}{124650432}\right)\ne(0,0).
\]
Thus \(P^\star\in\mathcal U\). Continuity supplies a relative neighborhood of \(P^\star\) inside the stated conditional-censoring, positivity, exact-rank, exact-transport submodel on which this nonzero discrepancy persists. Since the unadjusted estimator converges there to \(\theta+\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}\) rather than to the causal curve \(\theta\), the bias is fixed and does not vanish as \(K\to\infty\), completing the proof.

By the unit-factor-span condition and the displayed factorization of the pre-treatment matrices,
\[
y=v_n^\top U_0=w^\top VU_0=w^\top M.
\]
Thus \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:exact-rank} gives \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\), so the rank-\(r\) truncation satisfies \(M_r=M\) and hence \(M_r^+=M^+\).

For completeness, take a thin singular-value decomposition
\[
M=U\Sigma R^\top,
\]
where \(U^\top U=R^\top R=I_r\) and every diagonal entry of \(\Sigma\) is strictly positive.  The Moore--Penrose inverse is
\[
M^+=R\Sigma^{-1}U^\top,
\qquad
M^+M=RR^\top.
\]
Since \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)=\operatorname{row}(R^\top)\), there exists \(b\in\mathbb R^r\) such that \(y=b^\top R^\top\).  Therefore
\[
yM^+M=b^\top R^\top RR^\top=b^\top R^\top=y.
\]
The post/pre time-factor-span condition and the other displayed factorizations yield
\[
B=VU_1=VU_0A=MA.
\]
Combining the preceding identities gives
\[
yM_r^+B
=yM^+MA
=yA
=v_n^\top U_0A
=v_n^\top U_1.
\]
The last quantity is the latent untreated target-post grid under the latent-factor restrictions stated in the proposition.  Hence the observed-law spectral functional equals that causal curve because of the stated span restrictions, rather than by definition.

y=(7/10,9/20),

d=2,
\qquad
V=I_2,
\qquad
U_0=M,
\qquad
U_1=B,
\qquad
A=M^{-1}B,

\begin{pmatrix}7/10&2/5\\1/2&1/5\end{pmatrix}
